profile.bmw_cas4.source.0: Xhorse VVDI, Tips and Info about MC9S12XE Chip: BMW CAS4+ uses the whole 32 KB as D-Flash and has no EEE. https://www.xhorsevvdi.com/service/tips-and-info-about-mc9s12xe-chip.html
profile.bmw_cas4.source.1: CAS EEPROM notes: CAS4 version 1 is MC9S12XDP512 with a 4 KB EEPROM; version 2 is MC9S12XEP100 with a 32 KB D-Flash record layout that is not this EEE journal. https://tuning.wales/technical/cas-editor
profile.bmw_cas4.summary: CAS4 version 1 (MC9S12XDP512, mask 1L15Y) stores its data in a real EEPROM, not in S12XE D-Flash emulation. CAS4+ / version 2 (MC9S12XEP100, masks 5M48H and 1N35H) is partitioned as 32 KB of user D-Flash and no EEE. Replaying this tool's EEE journal against either file would invent an image the module does not use.
profile.bmw_cas4.title: BMW CAS4 / CAS4+
profile.bmw_cas4.vehicles: BMW CAS4 and CAS4+ access modules. Not an FRM, and not an EEE journal of the FRM kind.
profile.bmw_cas4.write_notes: Do not write a file from this tool to a CAS4 or CAS4+.
profile.bmw_frm3.source.0: Freescale AN3490, Overview of the MC9S12XE Emulated EEPROM: 32 KB D-Flash on the S12XEP100 (16K words), 256-byte sectors, two-word sector header, 63 data records per sector, DFPART/ERPART partition rule. https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN3490.pdf
profile.bmw_frm3.source.1: UPA-S footwell manual for MCU MC9S12XEQ384: D-Flash 32 KB, EEE up to 4 KB, example partition EEE 16 pages and D-Flash user 0. https://www.ecupinout.com/public/STD_FRM_MCU-9S12XEQ384_OSC8_4.75v_ConnStd4.pdf
profile.bmw_frm3.source.2: Xhorse VVDI, Tips and Info about MC9S12XE Chip: every MC9S12XE D-Flash is 32 KB; giving it all to EEE yields 4 KB, and the BMW E-chassis FRM is the example. A lost partition must be read as 32 KB D-Flash and converted. https://www.xhorsevvdi.com/service/tips-and-info-about-mc9s12xe-chip.html
profile.bmw_frm3.source.3: VVDI Prog FRM repair note: read MC9S12XEQ384 with EEE 0 / D-Flash 128 sectors, convert, write partition EEE 16 sectors / D-Flash 0. E-series script is XEQ384; F-series script is listed separately as XET512. http://blog.vvdishop.com/repair-bmw-frm3-xeq384-with-vvdi-prog/
profile.bmw_frm3.source.4: This repository: the original decoder and the ci/ sample pairs (32 KB D-Flash, 4 KB EEPROM), including the FRM3 field strings in ci/input/logs.
profile.bmw_frm3.summary: The whole 32 KB D-Flash is the EEE journal for a 4 KB emulated EEPROM. When the partition is lost the programmer can only read the raw 32 KB; replaying it rebuilds the 4 KB image the module used to expose as EEPROM.
profile.bmw_frm3.title: BMW / Mini FRM3
profile.bmw_frm3.vehicles: BMW and Mini FRM3 / FRM3R footwell modules whose programmer script is the E-series MC9S12XEQ384 (VVDI: FRM-E-SERIES-XEQ384). A published walk-through uses an E71. If the programmer identifies the part as F-series MC9S12XET512, use the experimental F-series profile.
profile.bmw_frm3.write_notes: Write the partition as user D-Flash = 0 sectors and EEE = 16 sectors (4 KB). That erase destroys the D-Flash copy, so keep the original dump. Program this file into the EEE / EEPROM area, not back into D-Flash, and verify the read-back. The image does not clear fault memory, short-circuit counters, mileage or checksums.
profile.bmw_frm_f_xet512.assumptions: No public repair note used here states the F-series script's D-Flash size, EEE size or DFPART/ERPART. The numbers above are copied from the E-series FRM3 (32 KB D-Flash, 4 KB EEE, DFPART 0, ERPART 16) so a tech can compare them with the programmer. They are not a confirmed F-series memory map. VVDI Prog 4.6.8 added FRM-F-SERIES-XET512 as a separate script and, in the same article, associates mask 2M25J with both that name and 9S12XEQ384.
profile.bmw_frm_f_xet512.source.0: VVDI Prog FRM repair note, F-series script named separately from the E-series XEQ384 script. http://blog.vvdishop.com/repair-bmw-frm3-xeq384-with-vvdi-prog/
profile.bmw_frm_f_xet512.source.1: Freescale AN3490 for the shared S12XE record system. https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN3490.pdf
profile.bmw_frm_f_xet512.summary: Runs the same S12XE journal replay as FRM3. No FRM3 VIN or part-number fields are decoded, because those offsets were only checked on the E-series samples.
profile.bmw_frm_f_xet512.title: BMW FRM F-series (XET512 script)
profile.bmw_frm_f_xet512.vehicles: Footwell modules that VVDI Prog lists under FRM-F-SERIES-XET512 rather than FRM-E-SERIES-XEQ384. The same VVDI note also labels mask 2M25J as 9S12XEQ384, so the die name is not settled.
profile.bmw_frm_f_xet512.write_notes: Do not program the image unless the programmer's own partition screen shows 4 KB EEE and 0 user D-Flash. If it shows another size, stop and keep the backup.

profile.jlr_kvm.assumptions: Xhorse and the CG100 KVM procedure agree the partition is 4 KB user D-Flash (DFPART 16) and 2 KB EEE (ERPART 8). They do not say whether those 16 user sectors sit at the start or the end of a raw 32 KB dump, and AN3490's extracted text does not settle the order either. This profile therefore scans all 128 sectors. Sectors that are not EEE records are warnings, not hard errors, because the user D-Flash is expected to be inside the same file. Unknown commands inside a real EEE sector are still errors. The 2 KB output is unverified against a KVM dump.
profile.jlr_kvm.source.0: Xhorse VVDI, Tips and Info about MC9S12XE Chip: Land Rover KVM is 4 KB D-Flash and 2 KB EEE, security byte FC, and must be unlocked before the EEE can be read. https://www.xhorsevvdi.com/service/tips-and-info-about-mc9s12xe-chip.html
profile.jlr_kvm.source.1: CG100 Jaguar/Land Rover KVM reset on Motorola 9S12XEQ384: adjust DFLASH 4K, EEPROM 2K. https://blog.uobdii.com/jaguar-land-rover-kvm-reset-cg100-can-read-write-9s12xeq384/
profile.jlr_kvm.source.2: VVDI Prog Land Rover RFA note: MC9S12XEQ384 D-Flash and EEPROM, masks including 1M12S. http://blog.xhorsevvdi.com/vvdi-prog-read-land-rover-rfa-1m12s-ok/
profile.jlr_kvm.source.3: Freescale AN3490 partition rule: (128-16)/8 = 14, which is a legal S12XE partition, and the record system is the family EEE. https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN3490.pdf
profile.jlr_kvm.summary: Published partition is 4 KB user D-Flash plus 2 KB EEE. A healthy locked module does not yield a plain EEE image; the chip has to be unlocked first. This profile replays a raw 32 KB read into a 2 KB image, using the top of the 4 KB buffer (words 1024-2047), the same window as the XF BCM.
profile.jlr_kvm.title: Jaguar / Land Rover KVM (RFA)
profile.jlr_kvm.vehicles: Keyless Vehicle Module / Remote Function Actuator on Jaguar and Land Rover, the module programmer menus call KVM or RFA. Not the XF body BCM.
profile.jlr_kvm.write_notes: Unlock before reading (Xhorse notes the security byte FC). The published write-back partition is D-Flash 4 KB and EEPROM 2 KB. Do not program this image until it has been compared with a known-good module of the same hardware. Verify after writing.
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.source.0: Jaguar Forum, BCM repair: XF emulated EEPROM is restored with this project's D-Flash replay, and the partition used was 2048 bytes EEPROM and 0 D-Flash. https://www.jaginfo.org/threads/bcm-repair.117049/page-7
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.source.1: Jaguar Forum, XF key-not-found: original allocation described as 2048 bytes EEPROM and 0 bytes D-Flash, with the whole 32 KB D-Flash backing that EEPROM. https://www.jaginfo.org/threads/problem-with-jaguar-xf-key-not-found.117470/page-4
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.source.2: Jaguar Forum, BCMB dump rewrite: XF rear BCMB CX23-14D628 on MC9S12XET256; facelift DX23 partition described as 2 KB EEE and 0 D-Flash. https://www.jaginfo.org/threads/bcmb-dump-rewrite.118137/
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.source.3: MHH AUTO, 2013 Jaguar XF BCM: MC9S12XET256, repair partition emulated EEPROM 8 x 256 and D-Flash 0. https://mhhauto.com/Thread-2013-JAGUAR-XF-BCM-FAULTY-DUE-TO-BATTERY-DISCONNECTION
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.source.4: Xhorse VVDI, Tips and Info about MC9S12XE Chip: D-Flash on the MC9S12XE series is 32 KB. https://www.xhorsevvdi.com/service/tips-and-info-about-mc9s12xe-chip.html
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.source.5: Freescale AN3490 Figure 2 and section 4.2: buffer RAM is 4 KB at 0x13_F000-0x13_FFFF, and each record's address label is the EEE RAM word address in that buffer. ERPART 8 and DFPART 0 meets the size rule and is 2 KB of EEE RAM. https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN3490.pdf
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.source.6: Freescale AN3743 Figure 6: ERPART regions are taken from the top of the buffer. ERPART 1 is the 256 bytes at 0x13_FC00-0x13_FFFF, so ERPART 8 is 0x13_F800-0x13_FFFF. https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN3743.pdf
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.summary: The XF BCM gives the entire 32 KB D-Flash to the EEE journal and emulates 2 KB (ERPART 8). The record's low 11 bits are the word address in the 4 KB buffer RAM at 0x13_F000-0x13_FFFF. A smaller ERPART occupies the top of that buffer, so this image is words 1024-2047 (bytes 0x800-0xFFF of a 4 KB replay), not words 0-1023.
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.title: Jaguar XF BCM / BCMB
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.vehicles: Jaguar XF (X250) front BCM and rear BCMB. Published part numbers include rear BCMB CX23-14D628-AE / AF and the later DX23 units, and front modules in the 14B476 part family. This is not the KVM/RFA.
profile.jlr_xf_bcm.write_notes: Partition to EEE = 8 x 256 (2048 bytes) and user D-Flash = 0, then write this 2 KB file to EEPROM, not to D-Flash. Verify the read-back. The file is the top 2 KB of the 4 KB buffer (global 0x13_F800-0x13_FFFF). Key programming and configuration can still require JLR SDD.
